reading.body:
Idaho's tracked 2026 bills concentrate on a handful of specific AI applications: a Conversational AI Safety Act, generative AI provisions for public education, AI review of administrative rules, AI in medical services, and unbiased AI requirements for state government purchasing, alongside three separate bills on programmable money.

The presence of a dedicated Conversational AI Safety Act, distinct from the state's social media and biometric identifier bills, indicates Idaho's legislature is treating chatbot and conversational AI systems as a category warranting its own safety framework rather than folding them into general technology regulation.

A companion bill revising penalties for disclosing explicit synthetic media sits alongside the addictive social media act, connecting Idaho's AI legislation to the same child and consumer protection concerns seen in other states' bill lists.

The data does not indicate which of these 14 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so Idaho's actual enacted AI framework is not established by this record.
